request.query: How do I enable my Applications to show up in the App Health view for the WAS agent?

limitations: 文档数是词项匹配的知识库覆盖计数，不是工单量、故障率、用户数、产品使用量或销售指标。

payload.answer:
(1) Right click on Application Health navigator item in the TEP 
(2) Select 'Situations' and then select 'WebSphere App Server' 
(3) Click on the icon to set Situation filter criteria (4 downward pointing arrows icon) 
(4) Tick the box 'Eligible for association' and select OK 
(5) Right click on WasAppDiscovered and select 'Associate' 
(6) Ok the situations box and close

You should be able to see all discovered applications at once in the Application Health Summary view at this point.

Alternatively you can run the Take Action Set_Application_Monitoring on specific applications this way: 

- Access the TEP, select the Navigator item "Application Health". Right click on this navigator item and select workspaces and then the workspace "Application Registry". 
- Right click on the applications that are presented and have a status of disabled or discovered in the view then select "take action". 
- Select the take action "Set_Application_Monitoring". All of the values for the take action will be filled in automatically. Change the value Mon_Status from 0 to 1 to enable Application monitoring. [S1]

source_lineage.excerpt:
(1) Right click on Application Health navigator item in the TEP 
(2) Select 'Situations' and then select 'WebSphere App Server' 
(3) Click on the icon to set Situation filter criteria (4 downward pointing arrows icon) 
(4) Tick the box 'Eligible for association' and select OK 
(5) Right click on WasAppDiscovered and select 'Associate' 
(6) Ok the situations box and close

You should be able to see all discovered applications at once in the Application Health Summary view at this point.

Alternatively you can run the Take Action Set_Application_Monitoring on specific applications this way: 

- Access the TEP, select the Navigator item "Application Health". Right click on this navigator item and select workspaces and then the workspace "Application Registry". 
- Right click on the applications that are presented and have a status of disabled or discovered in the view then select "take action". 
- Select the take action "Set_Application_Monitoring". All of the values for the take action will be filled in automatically. Change the value Mon_Status from 0 to 1 to enable Application monitoring.

ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  Environment:
   DC/TEMA ITCAM for J2EE v6.1.0.4
   OS Information: RHEL 4 UP6
   App Server: Weblogic 9.2
   
   Steps to reproduce:
    Step 1: Restart weblogic server
    Step 2: login TEP client
    Step 3: Choose enterprise->Linux Systems->h1.xyz.com->J2EE
   Agent - Primary-> BEA Weblogic App Server-
   Adminserver->Application Health
           Step 3: There are 7 applications listed in application
   health summary view
    Step 4: run some workload with WSWS using 1-5 clients
    Step 5: Wait for some time (several intervals), no data
   displayed in application health summary view in appliation
   health summary workspace

QUESTION
 How can I configure the CPU Consumption graph on Lifecycle Query Engine (LQE) Health Monitoring for IBM Jazz Reporting Service (JRS)? 

CAUSE
The CPU Consumption graphs always show zero. 

When you look at the LQE Health Monitoring Details you see that the CPU Consumption graphs showing 'LQE Application CPU' and 'Total System CPU' show zero. When you select 'View As A List' you will only see "Unavailable".
[/support/docview.wss?uid=swg22010666&aid=1] [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg22010666&aid=1]

[/support/docview.wss?uid=swg22010666&aid=2] [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg22010666&aid=2]

The values are not captured as it is not enabled when the LQE server is started.

By default baselining gets enabled with a situation WasAppDiscoverd. This situation is enabled by default and will discover new applications then run a take action to start the baselining. So if this situation is not enabled then you should enable it and assign to the ITCAM App Server managing system list. 

You want to do baselining with normal or typical load on the server over a period of few days to few weeks, or even few months. The performance of the application under this load is considered good (you will see "Good"" in the Application Health views) and deviation from this performance indicates degrading health ("Bad" or "Fair" in the Application Health views) of the monitored application. 

To start baselining for your application server, please follow these steps: 

(Note 1: in this example, I've used a WebSphere-based application but you can also do the same for any application on your J2EE agent also.)

For health checks configured to enter a warning or failed state, the information appears in the Health Summary as well as in the Notifications view. The Notifications view contains notifications from all of the Sites that are connected to your SiteProtector Console. To access the Notifications view, click the Notifications icon in the lower right of the SiteProtector Console.

=>Example : 

[/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21668033&aid=1] 


 0. Enter "co" 
1. When you enter "statistics", it will enable statistics on Data Power. This is necessary step to see data. 
2. "write mem" will save the configuration on Data Power. When you type "write mem", it will ask if you are sure that you want to save it. You enter "y". 

Note : Depending on the polling interval of the BN agent, it could take a couple minutes for the data to display. 

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 


 

PRODUCT ALIAS/SYNONYM
 ITCAM Agent for DataPower

SYMPTOM
No applications are showing in the Application Health workspace in the TEP for ITCAM for WebSphere


CAUSE
Applications were discovered but application monitoring was not enabled for any applications.

DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
Access the Application Registry workspace in the TEP and verify if you see application monitoring is set to disabled for any or all of the applications listed. 

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Access the TEP, select the Navigator item "Application Health". Right click on this navigator item and select workspaces and then the workspace "Application Registry". Right click on the applications that are presented and have a status of disabled or discovered in the view then select "take action". Select the take action "Set_Application_Monitoring". All of the values for the take action will be filled in automatically. Change the value Mon_Statusfrom 0 to 1 to enable Application monitoring. You should now see the applications in the "Application Health" workspace.
